card.name: Linking words before risk statements
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "and", "that", "but", "without" or a unit like "years", placed just before a statement about risk or outcome in drug-label warnings. One odd case is a capital P inside an uppercase Indonesian title.

modes.label: Linking word before risk
modes.description: A conjunction or "that" right before a clause about risk or treatability.
modes.example: generally consistent among drugs in the data analyzed. The finding of increased risk with AEDs of varying mechanisms of action and across a range of indications suggests<< that>> the risk applies to all AEDs

modes.label: Age range unit
modes.description: The word "years" ending an age range in a trial sentence about risk.
modes.example: indications suggests that the risk applies to all AEDs used for any indication. The risk did not vary substantially by age (5-100<< years>>) in the clinical trials analyzed. Table

modes.label: Contrast word
modes.description: "but" or "without" in a hedged risk phrase.
